title: fix(ci): expose timeout cancellations as failures

- Add a terminal `pipeline-status` job that runs with `if: always()` and observes every other job in `release.yml`.

title: fix(ci): gate manual releases on quality checks
body:
Fixes #119

## Problem

The manual `instant-release` and `changeset-pr` jobs had no dependencies, so they could begin writing to `main` before validation finished. In particular, an instant release could publish a broken package even when lint or tests failed later in the same workflow run.

There was a second dependency-path concern: `detect-changes` is skipped for `workflow_dispatch`, so simply adding `needs: [lint, test]` would leave the manual jobs permanently skipped unless the quality-gate conditions explicitly survive that skipped dependency.

## Solution

- Run `lint` for manual dispatches while preserving cancellation propagation.
- Run the test matrix for `instant` manual dispatches.
- Make `instant-release` depend on `lint` and `test`, and require both results to be `success`.
- Make `changeset-pr` depend on the faster `lint` gate and require a successful result.
- Keep `!cancelled()` in each condition so skipped transitive dependencies remain evaluable without allowing cancelled runs to write.
- Add a patch changeset.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before the workflow change, the new `manual release quality gates` tests fail because the writer jobs have no `needs`, lint/tests do not run on manual dispatch, and cancellation/result checks are absent.

The regression tests now evaluate the workflow conditions and verify that:

- successful lint and tests allow an instant release;
- either lint or test failure blocks publishing;
- changeset PR creation waits for successful lint;
- cancellation blocks both manual writer jobs.

## Testing

- `bun test --timeout 30000` — 203 passed
- `deno test --allow-read` — 172 passed

title: fix(publish): poll npm registry for verification instead of republishing
body:
Fixes #105

## Problem

`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` treated "publish succeeded" and "verification succeeded" as one retryable unit. When the publish worked but the single check 2s later missed because npm's registry had not propagated, the retry loop re-ran the whole `changeset publish`, which then failed with "cannot publish over the previously published versions" — turning a successful release into a reported failure.

## Solution

New module `scripts/publish-retry.mjs` splits the two failure domains:

- `waitForVersionOnRegistry()` — bounded polling with exponential backoff (7 attempts, 2s → 30s cap). A thrown E404/network error is treated as a miss and polling continues.
- `publishWithRetry()` — retries `changeset publish` **only** when the publish command itself failed. Once a publish reports success, the flow moves to verification and never re-enters the publish path; an exhausted poll fails the release without republishing.
- `isAlreadyPublishedError()` — `EPUBLISHCONFLICT` / "cannot publish over the previously published versions" is treated as a cue to verify, not to fail.

Verification is still mandatory: a publish that falsely claims success still fails the release.

`publish-to-npm.mjs` now delegates to `publishWithRetry`; `attemptPublish` became `runPublishCommand` (publish only, no verification). Non-retryable auth guidance from #77 is preserved.

## Reproduction / tests

`tests/publish-retry.test.js` encodes the scenario from the issue — a runner whose publish succeeds once and whose verification misses twice:

- one publish, verification eventually succeeds, success ✅ (previously: a second publish attempt and a conflict)
- exhausted verification polling fails without republishing
- publish-command failures still retry
- non-retryable auth errors still fail fast
- backoff sequence is capped at `maxDelay`

All 169 tests pass; `npm run lint`, `format:check` and `check:duplication` are clean.

title: ci: build Dockerfile on pull requests so a broken image fails the PR
body:
Fixes #106

## Problem

`docker-publish` (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is gated on `needs: [release, instant-release]` with `published == 'true'`, so the image is only ever built **after** the package is published. A Dockerfile regression cannot fail a pull request; it produces a half-finished release (package published, no image).

## Solution

New `docker-build` job that runs on pull requests with code changes, before any release job:

- `push: false` + `load: true` — works for fork pull requests, which have no registry credentials (`DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` is never referenced by this job).
- `cache-from/cache-to: type=gha` — shares the buildx layer cache with the publish build.
- `timeout-minutes: 30`, matching `docker-publish`.
- Reuses the existing `./.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient` action.

Because this template ships no Dockerfile by default, `scripts/check-docker-build.mjs` gates the build steps: no Dockerfile → the job succeeds as a no-op; Dockerfile present (path overridable via `vars.DOCKERFILE` / `vars.DOCKER_CONTEXT`, same variables the publish path uses) → the image is built. A missing build context is a hard error.

## Tests

`tests/docker-build.test.js` (new, 6 cases):
- the workflow job exists, needs `detect-changes`, is PR-gated, and has a timeout;
- it builds with `push: false` / `load: true` / GHA cache and never references `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`;
- it is not gated on the release jobs (the regression this issue reports);
- config evaluation: disabled with no Dockerfile (no error), enabled with one, error on a missing context.

`tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` updated with the new job's expected timeout.

Full suite: 162 tests passing across the node/bun/deno matrix locally; eslint + prettier clean. A changeset is included.

title: fix(publish): classify non-retryable npm failures and add NPM_TOKEN first-publish bootstrap
body:
## Summary

Fixes #77 — the npm release path failed slowly and unclearly on the **first
release of a brand-new package**, with two related root causes.

### Problem 1 — Permanent failures were retried `MAX_RETRIES` times

`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` treated every detected failure as retryable. But
`E404` (first publish of a package that does not exist yet),
`401`/`403`/`ENEEDAUTH`/`Access token expired` are **permanent** — retrying
wastes ~28s and hides the real cause behind a generic
`❌ Failed to publish after 3 attempts`.

**Fix:** A new `scripts/publish-failure-classifier.mjs` exposes
`isNonRetryableFailure()` and `buildAuthFailureGuidance()`. When a publish error
matches a non-retryable pattern, `attemptPublish()` flags it and the retry loop
**fails fast** with an actionable message explaining the first-publish
bootstrap, instead of retrying.

### Problem 2 — No first-publish bootstrap path (OIDC cannot create a new package)

npm trusted publishing requires a *trusted publisher* configured on npmjs.com,
which can only be done for a package that **already exists**. The first publish
of a brand-new package therefore cannot use OIDC and fails with `E404`.

**Fix:** Both `Publish to npm` steps (the `release` and `instant-release` jobs)
now pass an optional `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`. When
`NPM_TOKEN` is set, the first publish succeeds; once the package exists and a
trusted publisher is configured, OIDC takes over and the token can be removed.
Documented in `README.md`.

## How to reproduce the original issue

Run the release workflow for a scoped package that has never been published and
without a configured trusted publisher / token — npm returns `E404` and the old
script retried 3× before failing with a generic message.

## Tests

- `tests/publish-failure-classifier.test.js` — asserts E404/401/403/auth output
  is classified non-retryable, transient errors stay retryable, matching is
  case-insensitive and null-safe, and the guidance names the package +
  `NPM_TOKEN`/`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- `tests/workflow-reliability.test.js` — asserts both publish steps pass
  `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` as `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`.

All 84 tests pass locally (`npm test`); lint, format, and duplication checks are
clean.

title: ci: resilient buildx boot with mirror fallback for publish-dockerhub
body:
## Summary

`publish-dockerhub` booted buildx with `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` and no pinned-image pre-pull. The default `docker-container` driver pulls `moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1` straight from Docker Hub at boot, so a transient `registry-1.docker.io` outage failed the whole publish job — even with nothing wrong in the code or build.

This ports the resilient buildx boot pattern from `link-foundation/box` (issues #97 / #100) into this template.

## Changes

- **New composite action** `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient/action.yml`:
  1. Pre-pulls the pinned BuildKit image from canonical Docker Hub with retries + exponential backoff.
  2. On a full registry outage, falls back to `mirror.gcr.io` (Google's pull-through cache on independent infrastructure) and re-tags it to the canonical reference.
  3. Boots buildx with `driver-opts: image=…` pinned so the driver reuses the locally cached image and never touches the failing registry.
  4. Non-fatal fall-through if both sources are down (preserves prior worst-case behaviour).
- **`publish-dockerhub/action.yml`** now calls `setup-buildx-resilient` instead of `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4`.
- **`docs/case-studies/issue-75/CASE-STUDY.md`** documenting symptom, root cause, and fix.
- **Changeset** for a patch release.

## How to reproduce the original failure

Block `registry-1.docker.io` on a runner (hosts/iptables blackhole) and run the buildx step — the boot pull fails at *"Creating a new builder instance"*.

## Tests

- `tests/setup-buildx-resilient.test.js` extracts the real pre-pull `run:` block from the action and drives it with a mock `docker`, asserting recovery for: healthy registry (no mirror touched), registry-down/mirror-up (recovers + re-tags), and both-down (non-fatal warning). Runs in CI via `npm test`.
- `experiments/test-issue75-buildx-mirror-fallback.sh` is the standalone offline reproduction of the same scenarios.

All 18 suites / 75 tests pass; lint, format, and duplication checks are green.

Fixes #75

title: ci: add concurrency block to links.yml
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/links.yml` (Broken Link Checker) was the only workflow in this template missing a `concurrency:` block. Because it triggers on `push` (main) and `pull_request` like its siblings, pushing multiple commits in quick succession left redundant link-check runs in flight instead of cancelling superseded ones — wasting CI minutes.

This adds the same `concurrency` block already used by `release.yml` and `example-app.yml`, placed immediately after the `on:` section:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

The `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'` guard keeps the main-branch run from being cancelled mid-flight while still cancelling redundant PR/branch runs — consistent with the rest of the template.

## Summary

Closes #62.

Adds a release-time `preview-regen` job to `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` plus `scripts/update-preview-images.mjs` that boot the universal example app in a headless Chromium via `browser-commander` + Playwright, capture a locale × theme matrix of screenshots into `docs/screenshots/example-app/`, and commit drift back to `main` with `[skip ci]`.

Pattern reused from [konard/vk-bot-desktop#52](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/pull/52) (closes konard/vk-bot-desktop#51), adapted to this template's structure (Vite-built `examples/universal-app`, `@link-foundation/example-package-name` changeset).

## What's included

- **`scripts/update-preview-images.mjs`** — boots `examples/universal-app/dist` via a Node http static server, walks a 2×2 locale × theme matrix (`en`/`ru` × `light`/`dark`), drives Chromium through `browser-commander` (with verbose mode behind `PREVIEW_VERBOSE=1`), waits for `.app-shell` + `#calculator-title`, and writes `docs/screenshots/example-app/example-app-{locale}-{theme}.png`. Copies the `en-light` tile to `example-app.png` as the README fallback. `--skip-build` reuses any existing `dist`.
- **`preview-regen` job in `example-app.yml`** — runs on push-to-main and `workflow_dispatch`, installs `browser-commander@0.8.1` + `playwright@1.59.1` with `--no-save --package-lock=false` (so the root lockfile is not mutated), installs Chromium with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, regenerates screenshots, and commits any drift back to `main` with `[skip ci]` to avoid re-triggering itself.
- **`example:web:preview-images` npm script** — `node scripts/update-preview-images.mjs` for local repro.
- **Docs** — root `README.md` gains an "Auto-regenerated preview screenshots" section under "Deploying the example app" and a Scripts Reference row; `examples/universal-app/README.md` embeds the generated preview image with a note pointing at the workflow.
- **Test coverage** — new test in `tests/universal-app.test.js` asserts the npm script, workflow snippets (`preview-regen:`, `browser-commander`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `[skip ci]`), script imports (`from 'browser-commander'`, `from 'playwright'`), output path, and README snippets are all present.
- **Changeset** — `.changeset/preview-regen-pipeline.md` (`'@link-foundation/example-package-name': minor`).

## Why a 2×2 matrix when the example app has no i18n/themes yet

The script is template-ready: downstream forks that add a `data-theme` attribute or `lang` switching get matrix coverage without touching the script. `browser.newContext({ locale, colorScheme })` + `commander.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` plus a seeded `localStorage.theme` cover the common patterns. Today all four tiles render identically (114 520 bytes each), which is the documented baseline.

title: feat: add self-healing release pipeline for unreleased changes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #36

- Add `scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` — checks npm registry to detect unpublished versions, enabling releases even without changesets (analogous to Rust template's `check-release-needed.rs`)
- Update `release.yml` — integrate the new script as a self-healing fallback path in the release job
- Add case study documentation in `docs/case-studies/issue-36/`

## Problem

The release job was gated entirely on the presence of changeset files. If a PR merged without a changeset, the release job silently did nothing, leaving merged fixes unreleased indefinitely. This was documented in [link-assistant/web-capture#56](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/56).

## Solution

The new `check-release-needed.mjs` script runs after `check-changesets` and checks the npm registry:

1. **Changesets exist** → normal flow (`should_release=true`, `skip_bump=false`)
2. **No changesets, version not on npm** → self-healing (`should_release=true`, `skip_bump=true`) — publishes the current version directly
3. **No changesets, version already on npm** → no action needed (`should_release=false`)

The publish step in `release.yml` now has a third condition for the self-healing path:

```yaml
if: >-
  steps.version.outputs.version_committed == 'true' ||
  steps.version.outputs.already_released == 'true' ||
  (steps.check_release.outputs.should_release == 'true' && steps.check_release.outputs.skip_bump == 'true')
```

title: fix: use per-commit diff instead of full-PR diff for change detection
body:
## Summary

- **Per-commit diff instead of full-PR diff**: detect-code-changes.mjs now uses `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` for PR merge commits (GitHub Actions synthetic merge) to evaluate only what the latest push changed, not the entire PR
- **Remove unused env vars**: `GITHUB_BASE_SHA`/`GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` removed from workflow since merge commit detection is self-contained via `git cat-file`
- **Case study**: Root cause analysis with timeline, evidence from web-capture PR #49, and verification plan

Fixes #31

## Root Cause

Two separate issues were causing unnecessary CI runs:

1. **`GITHUB_BASE_SHA...GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` comparison** — the script compared the PR base against the PR head, giving the full PR diff (all files changed across the entire PR)

2. **GitHub Actions synthetic merge commit** — even `HEAD^..HEAD` gives the full PR diff, because GitHub creates a merge commit where `HEAD^` is the base branch

**Evidence**: In [web-capture PR #49](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/49), commit `0e9b6e8c` only modified `.gitkeep` but triggered all 8 CI jobs because the PR as a whole contained code changes.

## Solution

Detect the synthetic merge commit and use `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` (per-commit diff of the actual PR head):

```javascript
function isMergeCommit() {
  const parentCount = exec('git cat-file -p HEAD')
    .split('\n')
    .filter((line) => line.startsWith('parent ')).length;
  return parentCount > 1;
}
```

- `HEAD` = synthetic merge commit
- `HEAD^` = base branch (first parent)
- `HEAD^2` = actual PR head commit (second parent)
- `HEAD^2^` = PR head commit's parent

For push events, the regular `HEAD^..HEAD` is used.

This follows the same approach implemented and verified in [web-capture PR #51](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/51).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` | Replace full-PR diff with per-commit diff via merge commit detection |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Remove unused `GITHUB_BASE_SHA`/`GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` env vars |
| `experiments/test-detect-changes.mjs` | 17 edge-case tests for change classification logic |

title: feat: Add fresh merge simulation to CI/CD workflow
body:
## Summary

This PR incorporates best CI/CD practices from the [hive-mind repository](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind), specifically addressing the critical issue of **stale merge preview** in GitHub Actions.

### Key Changes

1. **Fresh Merge Simulation**: Added to both `lint` and `test` jobs in the CI workflow
   - Fetches the latest base branch when running PR checks
   - Merges it to simulate the actual merge result
   - Prevents stale merge preview issues where PRs pass CI but fail after merge

2. **Case Study Documentation**: Comprehensive analysis in `docs/case-studies/issue-23/`
   - Root cause analysis of GitHub's merge preview architecture
   - Timeline of events from hive-mind issue #1141
   - Online research on best practices
   - Raw data from referenced PRs for future reference

3. **Configuration Updates**:
   - Add ignore patterns for case study data files in ESLint and Prettier
   - Update lint-staged to suppress warnings for ignored files

### The Problem Being Solved

When a PR triggers a GitHub Actions workflow, GitHub creates a synthetic merge commit at `refs/pull/{number}/merge`. This is a **snapshot** that does NOT automatically update when the base branch changes. This leads to:

```
Day 1: PR opened -> CI passes (validates against snapshot)
[Time passes - other PRs merge to main]
Day N: PR merged -> Main CI fails (actual merge differs from snapshot)
```

### The Solution

The fresh merge simulation step ensures PR CI validates the **actual** merge result:

```yaml
- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
  run: |
    git fetch origin "$BASE_REF"
    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
    if [ "$BEHIND_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || exit 1
    fi
```

- [x] `npm run format:check` passes

- [x] `npm test` passes

- [hive-mind PR #1142](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/1142): fix: synchronize line count checks in CI/CD

Fixes #23

### Case Study Documentation

### 1. Automatic Package Root Detection
- Checks for `./package.json` first (single-language repo)
- Falls back to `./js/package.json` (multi-language repo)
- Supports explicit configuration via:
  - CLI: `--js-root <path>`
  - Environment: `JS_ROOT=<path>`

### 2. Fixed npm ERESOLVE Errors
- Added `--legacy-peer-deps` flag to all `npm install --package-lock-only` commands
- Ensures consistent behavior across workflow files and release scripts

### 3. Fixed Working Directory Corruption
- Save and restore `process.cwd()` after `cd` commands
- The `command-stream` library's `cd` is a virtual command that calls `process.chdir()`, permanently changing the Node.js working directory

### 4. Prevent False Positives in CI/CD (NEW - from PR #116)
Multi-layer failure detection in `publish-to-npm.mjs`:
- **Output pattern matching** for known error messages (`packages failed to publish`, `npm error code E`, etc.)
- **Exit code checking** (when available)
- **Post-publish verification** by querying npm registry

The `changeset publish` command exits with code 0 even when packages fail to publish. This is a known upstream issue ([changesets#1621](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/issues/1621), [changesets#1280](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/issues/1280)). Our multi-layer detection prevents false positive success reports.

```bash
# Auto-detection (default for single-language repos)
node scripts/version-and-commit.mjs --mode changeset

# Explicit configuration for multi-language repos
node scripts/version-and-commit.mjs --mode changeset --js-root js

JS_ROOT=js node scripts/version-and-commit.mjs --mode changeset
```

### Root Cause

When documentation-only PRs are merged without changesets:
1. The `changeset-check` job fails with "No changeset found"
2. The `lint` job depends on `changeset-check` succeeding
3. Prettier/ESLint never run on these PRs
4. After merge, the push to main triggers `lint`, which could fail on unformatted files

### Changes

**New Script:**
- Created `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` - a cross-platform Node.js script for detecting file changes in CI/CD
- Replaces need for inline bash scripts for better maintainability and cross-platform support

**Workflow Changes:**
- Add `detect-changes` job that runs the new script and outputs what types of files changed
- Make `lint` job **independent** of `changeset-check` - it's a fast check that should always run
- Make `changeset-check` **skip for docs-only PRs** by adding condition: `needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'`

2. **Docs-only PRs don't require changesets** (reducing friction for documentation updates)
3. **No differences between PR checks and push/merge checks** (preventing future surprises)

   - Refactored to reduce complexity by extracting helper functions

2. **Add `merge-changesets.mjs`**

   - Uses the highest version bump type (major > minor > patch)
   - Preserves all descriptions in chronological order (by file modification time)

3. **Update `release.yml` workflow**

   - Add step to merge multiple changesets before running `changeset version`

4. **Add comprehensive tests**

   - Tests for bump type priority, chronological ordering, edge cases

5. **Add case study documentation**
   - Timeline of events leading to the issue
   - Root cause analysis
   - Solutions and industry best practices
   - Reference data from hive-mind PR #961

### How It Works

**During PR validation:**
```
Before: Check all .changeset/*.md files → Fail if >1 exists
After:  Check only files ADDED in this PR → Fail if >1 was added
```

**During release:**
```
Before: changeset version → (fail if multiple changesets)
After:  merge-changesets.mjs → changeset version → (always single changeset)
```

1. **No more false failures** - PRs won't fail just because other PRs merged first

## Summary

This PR adds ESLint complexity checks with reasonable thresholds that encourage code maintainability without being overly strict, addressing the concern from #8 that the strict 50 lines per function limit was too restrictive.

## Implementation Details

Added the following ESLint complexity rules to `eslint.config.js`:

### Complexity Rules Added

| Rule | Threshold | Comparison | Rationale |
|------|-----------|------------|-----------|
| **complexity** | 15 | vs strict 8 | Allows moderately complex logic when needed |
| **max-depth** | 5 | vs strict 4 | Permits slightly deeper nesting for real-world scenarios |
| **max-lines-per-function** | 150 | vs strict 50 | More reasonable for orchestration and coordination functions |
| **max-params** | 6 | vs strict 5 | Allows additional parameters when justified |
| **max-statements** | 60 | vs strict 30 | Accommodates longer orchestration functions |
| **max-lines** | 1500 per file | vs strict 300 | Total line count including blank lines and comments |

### Configuration Details

All rules are configured at the **'warn'** level (not 'error') to:
- Provide helpful feedback to developers
- Highlight potential refactoring opportunities
- Avoid blocking development or causing CI failures
- Encourage but not enforce code quality improvements

For `max-lines-per-function`:
- `skipBlankLines: true` - blank lines don't count toward function limits
- `skipComments: true` - comment lines don't count toward function limits

For `max-lines`:
- Counts **all lines** including blank lines and comments (no skip options)
- The 1500 limit is the total physical line count of the file

This ensures that:
- Well-documented functions aren't penalized by documentation overhead
- File size limits are strict and count everything to maintain reasonable file sizes

## Testing

✅ All existing code passes the new complexity checks
✅ Local CI checks pass (`npm run check`)
✅ ESLint runs without errors or warnings
✅ Pre-commit hooks pass successfully

## References

- Fixes #9
- Related to #8 (effect-template best practices analysis)

## Comparison with effect-template

The effect-template repository uses very strict limits:
- 8 cyclomatic complexity
- 50 lines per function
- 4 max nesting depth

Our more lenient values (15, 150, 5 respectively) provide a better balance for this project while still encouraging maintainable code.
